title: Perf run 20261017-1252
eyebrow: 3D chess · perf-iteration · run 20261017-1252 · speed run, breakthrough
heading: A returning phone's start page is usable 28% sooner, and the computer searches about 40% faster
meta:
Two changes are kept. First, the host now lets a browser keep each built file for a year, and a click on the start page takes down a live preview that has loaded but not yet shown (ledger 0930:17, the change you approved with conditions). On a returning phone (4× slower CPU, Fast 4G) the start page is usable after 432 ms instead of 599 ms. The final A/B on 734d6d8 calls this better, with every pair between 0.67 and 0.82.

Second, the computer's board keeps the sums its evaluation reads as moves are made, and it tests whether a move leaves the king in check along only one line. Every search result is identical. The search-speed row went 52.9 → 32.3 ms, called better on 244a8a2. On the final commit it was −42% (8 pairs) and −44% (12 pairs, every pair faster), but the bench's rule did not call it either time (see Scoreboard). A review of a finished game took 2.81 s instead of 3.24 s, faster in every pair, not called.

The 1.2× target was met on 2 of the 8 headline rows measured. The run ran from 12:53 to about 19:40 UTC, about 6.8 hours against a budget of 6.

needs.intro: Nothing here blocks the PR. All three items are information; item 2 has a recommendation.

items.title: The 1.2× target was met on 2 of 8 rows (information)
items.body: On the final commit, against the base 1f207f0, 8 pairs (ab-20261017-1252-final.md): returning phone usable ×1.41 and search speed ×1.75 at the median pair met it; the review reached ×1.13. The other five rows measured are on the start page's first visit, which neither change speeds up. The seven game rows (moves, picks, a shared game, reopening, the first board pictures) were not re-measured: no code of this run runs there. Two breakthrough rounds tried six ideas for the search and the review; four did not pay (see Tried and rejected).

items.title: Hard may now play differently, because it searches to a clock (information)
items.body: The Hard level thinks for 1.8 s a move. With the faster search it now looks at about 20–40% more positions in that time, so it may choose different moves and play somewhat stronger. Easy and Medium are limited by depth, so they only answer sooner. Every test and fingerprint compares searches that stop at a fixed number of positions, so none of them shows this.
items.recommend: No action from you. The next general run plays new Hard against old Hard at equal time and retunes its time if the level moved (ledger 1017-1252:HS1).

items.title: Rows slower without a call, and the recorded costs of 0930:17 (information)
items.body:
• Start page usable, phone, first visit: 728 → 756 ms, median pair ×1.034, 5 of 8 pairs slower (1.08 0.98 0.93 1.04 1.05 1.20 0.97 1.03). Nothing in the diff runs on a first visit before the page is usable. An A/A on identical code leaned up to ±6% on a third of the rows.
  • Returning phone, your recorded cost: board on screen 584 → 674 ms (+8.3%, pairs 0.91–1.33, not called); first contentful paint +16%; connection open +15%; the instant first click 47.6 → 62.7 ms (within your +25 ms and under 100 ms). The returning script time until ready doubled (called worse, a diagnostic): the scene's chunk now comes from the cache and runs earlier. Winning these back is ledger RB1.

charts.caption: The returning phone's rows on the final commit, 734d6d8 against 1f207f0, 8 pairs (ab-20261017-1252-final.md).

scoreboard.intro:
The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. Target: each 1.2× faster than the base 1f207f0 (the dashed line). Over the 8 rows measured on the final commit the head is ×1.166 as fast; 1 row called better, none called worse.

The bench calls a change only when every pair agrees and the change is larger than the pairs' range divided by their mean. On the 12-pair search re-check every pair was faster (0.35–0.65), but one very fast pair made that range 55% against a 44% change, so the row was not called. That rule is logged as ledger 1017-1252:VR1 for a later run; it was not changed here, because changing it in the run whose win it would call is gaming the bench.

For the long view, the last measurement against the first recorded run (92ce041) stands: e02a235 was 2.48 times as fast over the 11 rows both can measure.

changed.intro: Each change below is a commit on the PR, with the A/B that called it.

items.title: A returning visit keeps the built files a year; a click takes down a preview that has arrived (c40494d, f16b8b5)
items.body:
The build writes a one-year immutable cache rule into _headers for each hashed file under assets/ (27 rules of the host's 100), adds assets/404.html, and fails on a file there with no hash or past 100 rules. A returning phone then loads the scripts from its cache without asking the server: 18 requests become 2. A click on the start page also takes down a live preview whose code has arrived but which has not shown, so its build does not run ahead of the next page. The bench fix c40494d makes the bench's server send the _headers the build wrote, as the host does; without it the change could not be measured.

Returning phone usable 581 → 427 ms, called better (ab-20261017-1252-cache.md); 599 → 432 ms, called better, on the final commit. Your three conditions held: the returning phone called better, the instant click +17 ms and under 100 ms, no first-visit row called worse.

items.title: The search keeps its evaluation's sums and tests legality along one line (e8d7472, 244a8a2)
items.body:
The computer's evaluation used to add up material, piece tables, game phase, bishops and king pressure over every piece at every position. The board now keeps these sums per move, updated by each move's change. A move other than the king's, made while not in check, can only expose the king along the line through the square it left, so legality is tested along that line only. Every search result is identical: the bench's fingerprint of the searches holds, and a 33-position fingerprint of move, score, depth and node count is unchanged. New tests compare the kept sums and each move's legality with a fresh count over about 50,000 moves of 12 random games.

Search speed 52.9 → 32.3 ms, called better; review 3.21 → 2.68 s, every pair better, not called (ab-20261017-1252-search.md, 244a8a2 against 2c97a27).

rows.change: 1017-0532:EV1+ (search: kept sums, line legality): 244a8a2 vs 2c97a27 (ai + review, 8 pairs)

items.title: A test that could not fail now can (734d6d8)
items.body: Each new check was run against a deliberately broken copy of the code. One break passed: removing the line that clears the mover's king pressure when it captures the king. The test's capturing rook stood four cells from the king, where the pressure is zero. It now stands two cells away, and that break and a stale recount after a king move both fail it. Removing only the click's flushSync also fails no test: React Router 8 already navigates in a transition, so the preview is taken down first anyway. The code is kept as measured; ledger CK1 decides the click half.

items.body: 2.47 → 2.11 s (−13%), 6 of 8 pairs better, not called (ab-20261017-1252-review.md). The four workers alone: −8.2%, 6 of 8, longest freeze during the review up. Reverted; patches/review-cores-start-RW1.patch.

items.title: M9: one set of search tables a thread, not 3.3 MB allocated per search
items.body: Search speed 31.7 → 29.1 ms (−11%), every pair better (0.74–0.99), but two pairs under 5%, so not called; review −5.4%, mixed (ab-20261017-1252-tables.md). Exact and a memory saving, so a general run can keep it: patches/search-tables-per-thread-M9.patch.

items.title: Bet 2: the review skips a deepening it predicts cannot finish
items.body: Killed on its probe by the criterion written before it. Over 101 positions, any rule that saves useful work changes answers: at the mildest setting 4 answers changed for −7% of positions searched. The next iteration can cost as little as a third of the last, because the transposition table carries work over.

items.title: MD1: mobility kept per move
items.body: Exact, but the review's work moved only −1% to −5% over two variants, under the 8% kill line. patches/mobility-delta-MD1.patch.

items.title: FG1, TT1 and a plain copy loop
items.body: FG1 (the move generator counts mobility on its walk): no gain, one case slower. TT1 (the table's move searched before the rest are generated): −1%, and not exact. A plain loop in place of copyWithin: no change.

items.title: RS1: a picked-up piece slower since 38d62be (closed as drift)
items.body: Three traced picks on each side showed no style recalculation or layout in any pick; the time is animation callbacks and waits on the GPU, with spikes on both sides. The 8-pair regression A/B leaned the other way (279 → 229 ms).

choices.intro:
• Took 0930:17 as measured, including a test extension the old ledger row said to drop (now ledger ST2), because you asked for the patch as measured.
  • Kept the click's flushSync, although no test needs it, so the shipped code is the measured code.
  • Ran the search re-check a second time with 12 pairs after the first's pair 1 read 1.00, decided before running to report it whatever it said. Both are committed; neither calls the row; the keep rests on the A/B that did.
  • Left the bench's calling rule unchanged (VR1).
  • Logged the review's other points (docs, hygiene, more checks, Hard's strength) for a general run instead of doing them in this speed PR.
  • Budget: about 6.8 hours against about 6.

notConfirmed.intro:
• That Cloudflare Pages answers a missing /assets/ name with assets/404.html and a 404, as ARCHITECTURE.md says. The live host was unreachable from here (ledger AH3).
  • The bundled node probe behind e8d7472's −18% on the review's work: its source was lost with the stage's scratch files and is not committed.
  • How much Hard's play changed (HS1).
  • The search-speed row on the final commit: every pair faster in both re-checks, but not called.
